chapter: Moving, Columbia Missouri and leaving home
title: Boogie-woogie, dance halls and Count Basie letting him sit in at Colorado Springs
summary: He learned from radio and records, chaperoned his sister at dances, and as a boy played on the bandstand when Basie was with Bus Moten.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: And at this time I learned from listening to the radio and records as much -- most jazz musicians do. And of course occasionally you would hear one of these orchestras that were coming through the city play for a dance. Of course now at this age, I was much too young to be admitted to dance halls. However, as I told you, as early as the time I was 12 years old in Colorado Springs, I used to go to dances and chaperone my sister, you might say. We were sort of chaperoning eachother. My sister would be allowed to
go out in the company of other boys, but I would sort of go along because I was interested in music and sort of a chaperone of hers, and because I played music they would let me come in.
And there was a time in Colorado Springs, Colorado when Count Basie was playing with Bus Moten, which you know the story of.

And they used to let me come up on the bandstand and play when my feet wouldn't touch the floor. Count Basie has mentioned this many times in his personal stories of me to other people, you know. And it was that early that I was trying to play this music, and evidently I must have been doing something that was interesting because in other words Basie let me come up on the bandstand and play. And plunk on the piano, as I would so do. Which, this was very interesting to the older people.
